title: Trump BLAMES Biden as Aviation Crisis Grounds America (ft. Maggie Haberman)
summary:
Jessica Tarlov is joined by New York Times reporter Maggie Haberman to break down the growing turmoil inside Trump’s administration, the fight over Democratic leadership, and why Trump may be losing support from the podcast crowd that helped elect him.

After thousands of flights were canceled and grounded nationwide and more than a million passengers were disrupted, the shutdown exposed just how urgently the country needs to modernize its decades-old air traffic control system.

But as the crisis unfolded, Trump was largely silent. While Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin faced reporters, the administration blamed Biden and demanded billions more in funding. Is Trump focused more on his legacy than the current state of affairs?

After a colossal midterms defeat, Trump is shaking up his cabinet. The president fired his chief of staff, Susie Wiles, earlier this month, replacing her with immigration hardliner Stephen Miller. Are more shakeups on the horizon? 

With Trump’s upcoming trip to China, there are some new questions about who will be in the president’s inner circle. How will the drama at Nvidia impact the meeting between Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin? 

There may be a serious challenge brewing to Chuck Schumer’s leadership: Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen. Is Van Hollen a credible alternative to Schumer for Democrats?
